mechanism_narrative: Higher housing starts (HOUST) signal a strengthening economy, which boosts corporate earnings and investor confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in high HOUST periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 6.0% signals a tightening labor market, which typically leads to higher consumer spending and corporate profits, driving equity prices up in the short term (5 days).
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of instances where UNRATE < 6.0% despite the negative signal, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds rate exceeds 0.5% and the CPI index exceeds 235, it signals a tightening monetary policy cycle that may lead to economic slowdown, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in < 40% of triggered instances, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime, a decline in industrial production (INDPRO < 102) signals an economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances (INDPRO < 102) during late-cycle expansion, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is associated with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, as it signals accommodative monetary policy that supports equity valuations.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in low FEDFUNDS periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A strong retail sales figure (RSAFS > 430,000) indicates robust consumer spending, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and corporate profits, driving short-term equity gains (5 days).
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in < 40% of instances where RSAFS > 430000, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Rapid labor force expansion (PAYEMS > 140000) combined with a low unemployment rate (UNRATE < 6.0%) signals a tightening labor market that may trigger inflationary pressures and monetary policy tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in < 40% of triggered instances, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime, a decline in quarterly GDP (GDPC1 < 18000) signals an economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances (GDPC1 < 18000) during late-cycle expansion, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
